title: Constraining the Chemical Signatures and the Outburst Mechanism of the Class 0 Protostar HOPS 383
question: Can the chemical signatures (N2H+ vs HCO+) and the disk mass/stability of the outbursting Class 0 protostar HOPS 383 constrain the outburst mechanism, e.g. gravitational instability?

what.value: Archival VLA centimeter flux densities of HOPS 383 added to the mm-cm spectrum (2014 data averaged, upper limits discarded)

evidence.quote: along with a few centimeter wavelengths data from the VLA archive reported by (cite: Madrid15)
From the archival data, we averaged the 2014 data and discarded the upper-limits

what.value: Dust opacity kappa(1.3 mm) = 0.899 cm2/g for thin ice mantles, used in the analytic disk mass

evidence.quote: We take $\kappa_{1.3 \text{ mm}} = 0.899$ cm$^2$g$^{-1}$ for thin ice mantles from dust opacity models of (cite: Ossenkopf94)

what.value: Mean Class 0 disk mass of 0.0078 Msun from 328 Orion protostars, used for comparison

evidence.quote: Based on the study of 328 protostars in Orion, (cite: Tobin20) found that the mean disk mass of Class 0 protostars was 0.0078 M$_{\odot}$.

what.value: Bolometric luminosity of HOPS 383, L_bol = 7.8 Lsun, used to scale dust temperature

evidence.quote: Also, (cite: Furlan16) found $L_{bol}$ of 7.8 $L_{\odot}$.

what.value: Earlier SED model luminosity 6-14 Lsun and inclination 41-63 deg

evidence.quote: found luminosities of 6 $L_{\odot}< L_{bol} <$ 14 $L_{\odot}$, and inclination of 41$^{\circ} < i < 63^{\circ}$.

what.value: Typical protostar mass of 0.5 Msun adopted for Toomre Q

evidence.quote: Using a typical protostar mass of 0.5 M$_{\odot}$ ((cite: Kenyon95))

what.value: Burst rate of 1 per 1000 yr inferred for a protostar in Orion

evidence.quote: (cite: Fischer19) inferred a burst rate of 1 per 1000 year for a protostar.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the ALMA 0.87 mm continuum
recipe.method: Manual calibration by the ARC node, CASA 4.7.2 self-calibration and Briggs weighted imaging

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux, disk size, position angle and inclination
recipe.method: Single-component Gaussian fit to the ALMA 870 micron continuum; inclination from arccos of the deconvolved minor/major axis ratio
key_parameters: Deconvolved FWHM 0.18'' x 0.12'', PA 49.7 deg; FWHM = 2.355 sigma

recipe.goal: Fit the mm-to-cm spectrum to separate dust and free-free emission
recipe.method: Power-law fit of the free-free emission to the long-wavelength points, subtraction from the 8 mm-1 cm data, then a dust power-law fit from 0.87 mm to 1 cm

recipe.goal: Estimate disk mass analytically from the ALMA and VLA flux densities
recipe.method: Optically thin isothermal dust emission mass formula with opacity scaled from 1.3 mm by a power law, times a gas-to-dust ratio of 100
assumptions: Dust temperature 30 K for typical low-luminosity protostar, scaled by (L/Lsun)^0.25 to ~50 K for L_bol = 7.8 Lsun
Opacity kappa(1.3 mm) = 0.899 cm2/g (Ossenkopf & Henning thin ice mantles), scaled as (1.3 mm / lambda)^beta

recipe.goal: Compute Toomre Q from the flux-derived disk masses
recipe.method: Q approx 2 M* H / (Md R) with a 0.5 Msun protostar, scaled by sqrt(T) for the pre-outburst temperature
assumptions: Disk radius R at which c_s is measured; the radius value adopted is not stated

recipe.goal: Fit radiative transfer disk+envelope models to ALMA and ALMA+VLA visibilities and the SED
recipe.method: RADMC-3D models (disk, Ulrich envelope with outflow cavity, protostar) with MCMC fitting using emcee, for truncated and exponentially tapered disks; Fourier transform of synthetic images to visibilities
key_parameters: Protostar temperature 4000 K; luminosity L* free
Dust: 60% silicate, 15% amorphous carbon, 25% porosity; minimum grain size 0.005 micron; envelope max grain 1 micron; disk max grain size and p (2.5-4.5) free
assumptions: Models constrain dust mass only; total mass quoted with gas-to-dust ratio of 100
Protostar mass used only to set the envelope density structure, not fit

recipe.goal: Compute Toomre Q versus radius and pre-outburst Q from the model profiles
recipe.method: Use model surface density and temperature (averaged over a few slices above midplane) in Q = c_s Omega / (pi G Sigma); pre-outburst temperature scaled by (L_pre/L_burst)^(1/4)
key_parameters: L*,pre = 0.5 Lsun; model-derived L*,burst; protostar masses 0.1 to 0.5 Msun

recipe.method: tau_dyn = D / V_flow (cos i / sin i) using the knot offset and line-of-sight velocity from the ALMA cube
key_parameters: closest knot 1.35'' from the protostar; V_flow ~ 10 km/s
assumptions: Knots travel at constant speed after ejection

answer_key.quantity: ALMA 870 micron integrated flux density

evidence.quote: The integrated flux density of HOPS 383 at 870 $\mu$m is 157.8 $\pm$ 3.2 mJy with peak intensity value of 47 $\pm$ 0.7 mJy/beam.

answer_key.quantity: VLA 8 mm integrated flux density

evidence.quote: the integrated flux density for the 8 mm wavelength data from the VLA is 411 $\pm$ 17 $\mu$Jy with peak intensity value of 290 $\pm$ 7 $\mu$Jy/beam.

answer_key.quantity: Disk radius from Gaussian fit to ALMA 870 micron

evidence.quote: The disk radius is estimated to be $\sim$62 au from Gaussian fitting of the ALMA 870 $\mu$m continuum enables.

answer_key.quantity: Deconvolved FWHM source size and position angle

evidence.quote: The deconvolved FWHM source size is 0.18$''$$\times$0.12$''$ and a position angle of 49.7$^\circ$; FWHM $\approx$ 2.355$\sigma$.

answer_key.quantity: Inclination from deconvolved size

evidence.quote: The deconvolved size also enables us to estimate the inclination of HOPS-383 to be $\sim$48$^\circ$ calculated from arccos($\theta_{min}$/$\theta_{maj}$).

answer_key.quantity: SMA Subcompact integrated flux densities at 0.85, 1.1, 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: In the Subcompact configuration, we obtained integrated flux density of 323.46 $\pm$ 12.7 mJy, 147.74 $\pm$ 12.2 mJy, and 136.63 $\pm$ 6.7 mJy at 0.85 mm, 1.1 mm, and 1.3 mm, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Free-free contribution at 8 mm, 9 mm, 1 cm

evidence.quote: The free-free contribution to the 8 mm, 9 mm, and 1 cm data is found to be $\sim$0.232 mJy, $\sim$0.234 mJy, and $\sim$0.237 mJy, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Dust power-law spectrum F_lambda,dust

evidence.quote: From the spectrum, we get the power law as $\text{F}_{\lambda, \text{dust}} = (0.17 \pm 0.08)\lambda^{-2.85 \pm 0.05}$ mJy

answer_key.quantity: Analytic disk mass from ALMA flux (T=30 K, 50 K; beta~1.78)

evidence.quote: we obtain disk mass of 0.082 M$_{\odot}$ and 0.043 M$_{\odot}$ for T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 30 K and T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 50 K, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Analytic disk mass from VLA 9 mm flux (T=30 K, 50 K; beta~1)

evidence.quote: we obtain total disk mass of 0.25 M$_{\odot}$ and 0.15 M$_{\odot}$ for T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 30 K and T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 50 K, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: VLA disk mass after free-free subtraction (T=30 K, 50 K)

evidence.quote: we get total disk mass of 0.11 M$_{\odot}$ and 0.063 M$_{\odot}$ for T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 30 K and T$_{\text{dust}}$ = 50 K, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Toomre Q from flux-derived masses (0.5 Msun protostar), for Md = 0.043 and 0.082 Msun

evidence.quote: we find that $Q = 1.67$ and 0.87 for M$_{\text{disk}} = 0.043 M_{\odot}$ and 0.082 $M_{\odot}$, respectively for the disk masses obtained from the ALMA flux density.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA-only model disk mass, inclination and position angle

evidence.quote: Both models have a protostellar disk mass of $\approx$0.02 $M_{\odot}$ and independently find the same inclination ($i \approx 51^{\circ}$) and position angle ($P.A. \approx 49^{\circ}$).

answer_key.quantity: ALMA-only model envelope masses and radii (truncated, tapered)

evidence.quote: Although the envelope masses (0.38 $M_{\odot}$ and 1.1 $M_{\odot}$) and radii (5700 au and 12000 au) differ between the truncated and tapered model

answer_key.quantity: ALMA-only model luminosity

evidence.quote: The luminosities of both models are very similar with $L \sim 5$ $L_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA+VLA model disk masses (truncated, tapered)

evidence.quote: The ALMA+VLA model results find massive disks of $M \sim 0.33 M_{\odot}$ and $M \sim 0.21 M_{\odot}$ for the truncated and the tapered cases, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: ALMA+VLA model envelope masses (truncated, tapered)

evidence.quote: The truncated disk model has a very similar envelope mass compared to the ALMA only models with $M_{env}$ = 0.32 $M_{\odot}$.
the tapered disk model has very low envelope mass of 0.09 $M_{\odot}$

answer_key.quantity: Radius of the 25 K temperature limit now (ALMA only, ALMA+VLA models)

evidence.quote: the ALMA only and the ALMA+VLA models have 25 K temperature limit at $\sim$550 au radius and $\sim$250 - 400 au radius, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Radius of the 25 K temperature limit before the outburst

evidence.quote: Before the outburst, the models have the 25 K temperature limit at a radius around 50 - 100 au

answer_key.quantity: Dynamical timescale of the closest outflow knot

evidence.quote: We get $\tau_{dyn} \approx$ 215 yr, with $V_{flow} \approx 10$ km/s

answer_key.quantity: Spacing between outflow knots

evidence.quote: which translates to roughly 1400 yr between the knots.

answer_key.quantity: Outflow position angle from SMA 12CO

evidence.quote: we determine the position angle (PA) to be about 137.5$^{\circ}$.

answer_key.quantity: Free-free to total 9 mm flux ratio and rescaled ALMA+VLA disk masses (truncated, tapered)

evidence.quote: the ratio of free-free emission to total flux density is 234 $\mu$Jy/411 $\mu$Jy $\approx 0.57$.
this gives us disk masses of $\sim$0.14 M$_{\odot}$ and $\sim$0.092 M$_{\odot}$ for the truncated and the tapered ALMA+VLA models, respectively.

score_reason: ALMA project code, CASA version, robust, flux calibrators and key analytic formulae with numeric results are given, so the continuum flux, size and analytic disk mass are reproducible; the radiative transfer modeling lacks priors, SED data and self-calibration detail, and the calibration was done manually.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project code is printed and the data come from the VANDAM survey; the continuum flux, Gaussian size, inclination and analytic disk masses are numeric and redoable, though the full RT model fit is not completely specified.
